children: Semiconductor manufacturer Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials) finished up 8% last week, a swift rebound from a severe Monday selloff. The company develops CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.

The bounce was notable as the Philadelphia semiconductor index gained just 0.8% for the week, vs a gain of almost 2% for Nvidia. AMD and Nvidia both plummeted in Monday's wider tech selloff but AMD recovered more sharply.

One catalyst arrived Thursday when Piper Sandler reiterated its Overweight rating and $600 price target, noting that CPU and GPU product launches were still on track and demand was still outpacing available supply.

That supply imbalance might also be giving AMD pricing power. The company said customers will be warned of approximately 10% price increases on some AI accelerators and GPUs in the fourth quarter, citing rising production costs as a reason, according to reports.
The combination is important for investors. This is supported by strong demand, and if prices are increased and customers continue to buy, revenue per unit could increase.

Wall Street's expectations are climbing as well. There were 55 analysts tracking AMD, with 39 Buy ratings, five Outperforms and 11 Holds, the source reported. The average target of $617 was around 10% higher than the stock's then-current price.
The next question is whether AMD can translate tight supply and pricing power into improved financial outcomes as its AI and data-center products ramp.

title: AMD's 8% Surge Hints at Something Bigger
